source_title: 'Ballot paper, still we ask': Kharge dares BJP to dissolve Parliament after MLC poll setback - The Times of India
source_excerpt: NEW DELHI: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge on Thursday reiterated the opposition's demand for voting using ballot paper despite the party's lacklustre performance in the Karnataka MLC elections, which were held using ballot papers.Reacting to the Karnataka MLC results, Kharge said the opposition would not give up its demand for ballot paper voting simply because BJP won the elections. He also challenged the BJP to dissolve Parliament and contest elections using ballot papers."Ballot paper, still we ask. It doesn't mean that we should leave because they are winning. Once upon a time they won only two Parliament seats. Sometimes it happens, that doesn't mean that party has no hold," Kharge said."That ego should not be there in BJP that they have done very well. If that is the case, let them dissolve the Parliament and go on ballot paper," he added.Kharge's remarks came after Prime Minister Narendra Modi took a dig at Congress for "drawing a blank" in recent MLC elections. The grand old party had won zero seats till Wednesday night. The party, however, opened its account after retaining Nagpur Division Graduates' constituency seat."MLC elections in 28 seats across 4 big states - Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Bihar and Karnataka. Elections held using ballot papers. Guess how many seats Congress won?" PM Modi said in a post on X.BJP national president Nitin Nabin also targeted Congress, saying the party would continue to struggle for survival under Rahul Gandhi's leadership.
